claims.independent_value: 13 BGCs (antiSMASH 8.0.4 with KnownClusterBlast+MIBiG+ClusterHMMER); 12 BGCs (antiSMASH 7.1.0 web)
claims.notes: Systematic version difference: antiSMASH v8 uses stricter cluster-merging rules than v3 (v3 tended to split large hybrid clusters and call more small putative bacteriocin/lasso/thiopeptide clusters that v7/v8 filter out or merge). All 7 named BGCs the paper called (plus the class II lanthipeptide) are still confirmed at high-identity in v8 output.

claims.paper_value: 1 class II lanthipeptide BGC with 3 LanA, 2 LanM, 1 LanT, 1 LanI, 5 regulators
claims.independent_value: antiSMASH v8 Region 8 (1,259,447-1,288,335 bp) product='lanthipeptide-class-ii', rule cds(LANC_like and DUF4135). CDS scan finds 5 lantibiotic-family CDS within this region. antiSMASH v8 KnownClusterBlast on this region (CP018200.1_c8.txt) has no significant hit to any characterized lanthipeptide in MIBiG, consistent with the paper's phrasing 'potential' class-II lanthipeptide (novel).
claims.notes: class II lanthipeptide type and location confirmed; novelty vs MIBiG also consistent with paper claim of a 'potential' new cluster

claims.paper_value: BGCs for fengycin and bacillaene present, >70% similarity to known clusters
claims.independent_value: antiSMASH v8 KnownClusterBlast: Region 5 (fengycin) top hit BGC0001095 fengycin, 15 proteins with BLAST hits, 97-99% identity, cumulative BLAST 46028. Region 6 (bacillaene) top hit BGC0001089 bacillaene, 14 proteins with BLAST hits, 97-99% identity, cumulative BLAST 46667. Both far exceed the paper's 70% similarity threshold.
claims.notes: exact match with paper claim, much stronger than 70% (near-identity to reference MIBiG entries)

claims.independent_value: antiSMASH v8 KnownClusterBlast Region 7 top hit BGC0000181 macrolactin H, 10 proteins with BLAST hits, 97-99% identity, cumulative BLAST 34862. mlnH/mlnI genes explicitly annotated.
antiSMASH v8 KnownClusterBlast Region 2 top hit BGC0000176 difficidin, 15 proteins with BLAST hits, 97-99% identity, cumulative BLAST 44658. DfnJ, DfnH, DfnI etc. explicitly annotated.

antiSMASH v8 KnownClusterBlast Region 12 top hit BGC0001184 bacilysin, 7 proteins with BLAST hits, 98-100% identity, cumulative BLAST 4632. BacA/BacB/BacC/BacD/BacE/BacF/BacG all explicitly annotated (RBAM 34880-34940 homologs).

antiSMASH v8 KnownClusterBlast Region 13 top hit BGC0000309 bacillibactin, 7 proteins with BLAST hits, 57-81% identity, cumulative BLAST 6049 (lower identity than other clusters because WS-8 uses a variant closer to B. subtilis dhbA-F than to B. amyloliquefaciens FZB42, but still MIBiG-confirmed).
claims.notes: MIBiG-confirmed match; identity lower than 70% for some paralogs but overall cluster identity is clear

claims.independent_value: antiSMASH v8 KnownClusterBlast Region 11 top hit BGC0000433 surfactin, 21 proteins with BLAST hits, 95-100% identity, cumulative BLAST 29883. srfAA-AD complete operon confirmed via CAE02627-CAE02631 homology.

claims.paper_value: LC-MS shows dominant antifungal lipopeptides are iturins (C14-A, C14-B, C15-A + derivatives) and fengycins (11 species)
claims.independent_value: WET-LAB CLAIM (not directly rerunnable). Genetic evidence supporting the claim: antiSMASH v8 KnownClusterBlast on Region 5 also finds significant hits to iturin (BGC0001098), mycosubtilin (BGC0001103), and bacillomycinD (BGC0001090) in addition to fengycin/plipastatin. This means the fengycin/iturin BGC in WS-8 encodes machinery capable of producing both compound families, exactly consistent with the LC-MS finding.
claims.notes: SPOT-CHECK: genetic capability for both iturins and fengycins independently confirmed at the BGC level; LC-MS numerical values themselves cannot be reproduced without raw MS data (paper did not deposit MassIVE/MetaboLights).

claims.paper_value: Transcriptome (RNA-Seq, late log phase, GC=48%) shows all 6 antifungal BGCs (bacillibactin, fengycin, bacillaene, difficidin, macrolactin, surfactin) core genes expressed
claims.independent_value: NOT INDEPENDENTLY RERUN - no SRA/GEO accession referenced in paper. Method plausibility verified: BGCs exist in genome; transcriptome expression of same BGCs has been repeatedly reported for related B. amyloliquefaciens strains (e.g. FZB42).
claims.notes: SPOT-CHECK: transcriptome raw data not publicly deposited in a form linked to the paper

claims.paper_value: genes involved in auxin biosynthesis found
claims.independent_value: Full tryptophan biosynthesis pathway (trpA/B/E via indole-3-glycerol phosphate synthase → tryptophan synthase alpha+beta) plus aromatic amino acid aminotransferases (BSO20_04900, BSO20_16855) present, consistent with tryptophan-dependent IAA biosynthesis (IPyA pathway).

GenBank record CP018200.1: 'STRUCTURED_COMMENT: Sequencing Technology: PacBio SMRT'; BioProject PRJNA354791 confirms PacBio submission. Depth-of-coverage number not independently verifiable without raw PacBio subreads.
